This Sprinter Proves a Camper Van Can Match a Normal Home's Comfort — But Also Go Off-Road
26 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans
Even more expensive older campers can be a bit lacking when it comes to design and amenities. But today's premium camper vans rise up to the comfort level of a conventional home. Of course, not all of them, but there are some builds, like the one I'd like to share today, that are incredibly practical.
Today's featured home on wheels is a conversion based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created by Papago Vans, a Mesa, Arizona-based company specializing in off-grid and off-road-ready camper vans.
Like with all Papago Vans rigs, you can tell straight away that you're looking at a camper van . For starters, the vehicle rides on bronze Black Rhino Outback wheels wrapped in Nitto Ridge Grappler all-terrain tires. The company went even further and upgraded the rig's off-roading capabilities by installing a Van Compass Stage 4.3 suspension kit, which comes with front and rear adjustable shocks and rear mini leaf springs.
At the front, you'll come across a CAtuned bumper complete with a hitch receiver. The opposite end of the van was also put to good use, as it has a spare tire carrier and another carrier with an Aluminess powered bike rack with two 1Up trays and a cargo box. The best part about the powered rack is that it makes loading and unloading your bikes much easier.
An FVC (Flatline Van Co.) ladder on the driver's side offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll find an FVC Safari rack holding a front-facing 50-inch LED light bar, a Nomadic Cooling A2 powered awning with integrated lights, light pods on the sides, and two 200 W Renogy solar panels. What's more, it has panels that cover it that can double as a deck.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Slide the door open, and AMP Research steps will deploy from underneath the van, and they go back under when you don't need them. Enter, and you'll be greeted by a homey, beautifully designed interior.
The customer opted for custom cream-colored laminated cabinetry, a tongue and groove ceiling with a darker finish, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by dark bamboo countertops and gold accents, such as the cabinet and drawer handles.
A key detail is that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space, creating a roomier feel.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. You can also set up a Lagun table to use the cabin as a seating area. What's more, the passenger seat base houses an Espar heater that taps directly into the vehicle's fuel tank.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans In the top part of the cabin, there's a large Van Essential headliner shelf with gear mounting points and a curtain rod. So, you can add a curtain to separate the two areas if you want, for more privacy and better insulation.
The kitchen is the first part of the living space, split into two units, one on each side of the van. It features a deep stainless steel sink with an insert and a filtered water faucet, a multi-function oven, and a 130-liter fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
You get plenty of meal prep space on the kitchen's two counters. If that's somehow not enough, you can use a large flip-up table to extend the passenger-side counter. It's also perfectly positioned to double as a table for the swiveled passenger seat.
A Maxxair vent fan above the kitchen will draw out the smells and fumes from cooking. By the way, to save counter space, the customer chose a portable induction stove instead of a fixed one.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans With this being a premium van, it's not a surprise that it offers one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: a bathroom, and quite a spacious one at that. It sits on the driver's side and boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a toilet, and a Nautilus self-cleaning retractable door. I'm also fond of its dark look, with the black shower, black door, and real grey-black tiles.
Three overhead cabinets, three drawers, and three lower cabinets are available for storage in the kitchen. There's also a floor-to-ceiling unit by the bathroom entrance that integrates two tall closets with multiple shelves.
The rear part of the living space is designed to offer as much comfort as possible - it's the perfect spot to relax after a day out adventuring, whether you want to lounge or sleep.
The bedroom offers a queen-size mattress, three overhead cabinets, and three storage compartments with hinged tops by the bed.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans You can also chill out and watch a movie thanks to a 24-inch smart TV attached to a swivel mount. Furthermore, the A/C unit above will quickly cool you off when needed.
The space underneath the bed was turned into a garage that can be accessed from both inside and outside the van. In its middle part, there are two FVC pull-out trays – they're attached to heavy-duty slides that can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg) and come with mounting points for strapping things down.
Two boxes on the sides accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 920 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter.
That's plenty of battery capacity to run the numerous power consumers in the van. Even better, you can use three charging sources to make sure you never run out of juice: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans If the electrical box gets too hot, a fan will turn on to push all that hot air out. The box also has a connection for an ARB air compressor, as well as outlets and switches for the garage lights and rear perimeter lights.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, a water filter for the sink, a 4-gallon (15-liter) Bosch electric water heater, and an outdoor shower connection. Both water tanks have heating pads.
The van's "brains," or, in other words, the control panel for the utilities, is located inside one of the kitchen overhead cabinets. It includes a tablet that lets you monitor and control the power system, as well as switches for the water pump, water heater, a freeze protection system, and the shower drain that pulls water into the greywater tank.
All in all, this Sprinter-based conversion by Papago Vans has it all, ready to go wherever the journey takes you. It cleverly combines a beautiful luxury interior with rugged off-road capability.
